# We are doing
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(here)
library(readr)
library(patchwork)
```


```{r}
# first step of the process
# raw data file
raw_data <- read_xlsx(here("pone.0302604.s004.xlsx"), skip = 1)
view(raw_data)

sig_variables <- raw_data %>% select(burnout,apathetic, self_compassion, compassion_fatigue, mental_wellbeing,depression,receptive,connectedness)

model.from.paper <- lm(burnout ~., data = sig_variables)
summary(model.from.paper)

```


Looking at the original paper

* The **burnout variable** is considered to be the target/predictor variable
* their first multiple linear regression model is fit using the variables that have p-values under 0.05 for t-tests regarding whether thevaliue of the coefficient is non-zero or not
  - these people do not seem to be treating the 0.05 significance level like a 'night' and 'day' thing
  
* they use the variables *apathetic*, *self compassion*, *compassion fatigue*, *mental wellbeing*, *depression*, *receptive*, and *connectedness*
* the $R^2$ in their model is 0.70, and they say that 70% of the variation in burnout scores is explained by the regressors, but again, this does not tell us anything about the appropriateness of the model fit.


```{r}
# manually creating their "S1 Table" for the number of online diary entries for each month
Months <- c("January 2021", "February 2021", "March 2021", "April 2021", "May 2021", "June 2021", "July 2021", " August 2021", "September 2021", "October 2021", "November 2021", "December 2021", "January 2022", "February 2022", "March 2022", "April 2022", "May 2022")
```

```{r}
# recreating the 'S1 Fig. Distribution'
# sig_variables$self_compassion <- sig_variables$self_compassion + 10.01


p1 <- sig_variables_no_10 <- sig_variables %>% filter(self_compassion != 10)
ggplot(data = sig_variables_no_10, aes(x= self_compassion)) + geom_histogram(bins = 10, color = "red") + labs(x = "Self-Compassion Scores", y = "Counts", title = "S1 Fig. Distribution")
p2 <- sig_variables_no_10 <- sig_variables %>% filter(self_compassion != 10)
ggplot(data = sig_variables_no_10, aes(x= self_compassion)) + geom_histogram(bins = 10, color = "red") + labs(x = "Self-Compassion Scores", y = "Counts", title = "S1 Fig. Distribution without score 10")

p1+p2
```
